result:
The lookup was exposed because patient search sent no caching-strategy header, so the service worker treated each request as needing a dynamic-route lookup. The fix was PR #2638, which added an explicit header to patient search requests. Offline support has since been removed, so the header is gone too.

**Why the lookup was exposed.** The service worker's default handler only skipped the route scan when a request carried the `x-omrs-offline-caching-strategy` header. Without it, `getHandlerKey` fell through to `getHandlerKeyFromDynamicRouteRegistrations`, which opened `ServiceWorkerDb` and read every dynamic route registration on each request (`openmrs-esm-core`, `packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/service-worker/routing.ts`, lines 84–113 at `a62f8164^`; the file was deleted by `a62f8164`). Patient search's fetchers were plain `openmrsFetch` calls, so every search paid that cost. PR #2638 describes it as "an expensive per-request Dexie lookup that was unnecessarily slowing things down."

**What the requests did after #2638.** Patient search's `fetcher` sent `x-omrs-offline-caching-strategy: network-only-or-cache-only` on the infinite search, recently-viewed user and REST patient requests (`patient-search.resource.tsx`, diff of `e4aacbd5`). The explicit header short-circuited the route scan, so those requests went to the network and fell back to cache only if that failed.

**Current state.** Offline support was removed later: patient management in `81c24905` (#2776, 2026-09-25) and the framework in `a62f8164` (#1894, 2026-09-28). At HEAD the patient search `fetcher` is a plain `openmrsFetch` with no header, and no service worker handles these requests. The lookup no longer pays the dynamic-route cost because there is no service worker left to pay it.

**Change and ticket:** PR #2638 (merge commit `e4aacbd5`), ticket O3-5832. Falkon's ticket link is verified and the PR body names O3-5832.
